identity.name: Active Clothing Co  Limited
identity.industry: Apparel / Smart Manufacturing & Global Supply Chain Integration

summary.oneLiner: Active Clothing is scaling India's first knit-to-shape smart factory with 600 new machines to future-proof against US trade volatility, but near-term margins are pressured by temporary labor cost inflation and market uncertainty; the real catalyst is the 2027 commissioning of this facility, which could unlock Rs.700Cr revenue potential.

one-line thesis: Active Clothing is scaling India's first knit-to-shape smart factory with 600 new machines to future-proof against US trade volatility, but near-term margins are pressured by temporary labor cost inflation and market uncertainty; the real catalyst is the 2027 commissioning of this facility, which could unlock Rs.700Cr revenue potential.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +1.65% YoY (Q2), +15.22% YoY (H1); EBITDA/margin: 8.88% (Q2), 9.72% (H1) — Q2 dip due to labor cost inflation; PAT (rptd): Rs.2.79Cr (Q2), Rs.4.92Cr (H1); PAT (normalized): same — no one-offs; Order book: Rs.15Cr from San Francisco/Levi’s; Net debt: stable — Rs.60Cr capex funded via supplier credit, no new debt raised
guidance: Revenue growth: targeting Rs.700Cr total revenue post-600-machine rollout; Margin: expected to improve post-2027 automation efficiency gains; Order inflow: new audits underway with Primark, Marks & Spencer; Capex/commissioning: Rs.60Cr in FY26-27; full 600-machine rollout over 3 years (2027 end)
order book & pipeline: Rs.15Cr from Levi’s San Francisco division; additional sampling approved for Agilitas; Primark and M&S audits in progress (expected onboarding in 3-4 months)
segment / subsidiary detail: Sweaters: largest segment; Jackets & woven: growing; T-shirts & uppers: moderate; Export revenue: crossing Rs.100Cr in FY26; Domestic: ~75% of revenue; No new product categories — expansion within existing lines
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into European markets (UK, Germany); Potential entry into mass-market brands (Primark, M&S); Leveraging 3D design tech to attract new global clients; Long-term revenue upside to Rs.700Cr post-capex completion
margins & cost dynamics: Q2 EBITDA margin dipped to 8.88% due to 8% YoY employee benefit cost increase (wages + benefits) — temporary labor inflation from retention needs amid market uncertainty; Raw material (cotton/yarn) stable; Margin recovery expected post-automation efficiency gains (labor + waste reduction) from 2027
capex / expansion: Rs.60Cr in FY26-27 for infrastructure; Full 600-machine project cost: Rs.150-200Cr; Supplier (Ningbo) provides machinery on 5-year deferred payment — no equity/debt raise needed; Rs.50Cr of Rs.60Cr capex is machinery cost
capital allocation: 100% focused on capex for smart knitting machines; No dividends or buybacks mentioned; No new debt raised; Supplier financing eliminates need for external capital; Working capital managed efficiently (positive OCF)
risks & watch-items: US tariff uncertainty impacting demand visibility; Slow adoption in new European markets; Competitive pressure from displaced Chinese/other Indian suppliers; Execution risk in 3-year machine rollout; Labor cost inflation if wage hikes persist beyond 2026
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic — framing US trade disruption as temporary, emphasizing automation as non-negotiable future, highlighting supplier financing as a strength, projecting Rs.700Cr revenue target with clear roadmap; tone is optimistic but grounded in operational discipline
non-obvious takeaways: The Rs.60Cr capex is not a cash outflow — it’s supplier-financed machinery; the real capital risk is borne by Ningbo, not Active Clothing; this is a rare case of capex being funded by equipment vendor — a structural advantage
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| American market disruption due to tariffs | Other Indian apparel manufacturers | loser | High | Active is less exposed than peers (only 25% export to US), and is using the disruption to build automation moat — competitors without capex will lose market share |
| Rising labor costs and retention pressure | Active Clothing Co Limited | winner | Medium | Labor cost inflation is temporary and being offset by automation — company is investing in retention to secure skilled workforce for future smart factory |
